item.title: Civil Rights photojournalist visits IC during annual MLK celebration
item.description: On Feb. 11, Ithaca College hosted its annual Martin Luther King Jr. keynote address as part of the campus wide MLK Celebration Week during Black History Month. The 2026 guest speaker was Cecil J. Williams, a South Carolinian Civil Rights leader, photojournalist, author and historian. The post Civil Rights photojournalist visits IC during annual MLK celebration appeared first on The Ithacan.

item.title: Students rethink sleep in spring semester
item.description: With the spring semester in full swing, students at Ithaca College are reconsidering their sleep schedules. Winter brings about a host of changes: new schedules, less sun and colder months keeping everyone inside. Sleep often changes as well. The post Students rethink sleep in spring semester appeared first on The Ithacan.

item.title: Fellowship of Christian Athletes combines love for faith and the field
item.description: In a small college of approximately 4,700 students, students create many ways for their peers to engage in a niche community. Every Tuesday night in the Athletics and Events Center, the Ithaca College chapter of Fellowship of Christian Athletes provides over 50 students with an opportunity to gather and share two intertwined passions: sports and their Christian faith. The post Fellowship of Christian Athletes combines love for faith and the field appeared first on The Ithacan.

item.title: IT policy changes prompt community reaction
item.description: The Ithaca College Information Analytics and Technology team released an updated version of its IT policy Jan. 30, following multiple phishing attempts. The changes include new guidelines for the use of IC emails by faculty, staff and students, prompting mixed reactions from the community. The post IT policy changes prompt community reaction appeared first on The Ithacan.

item.title: Professors publish article on importance of indigenous cultures in higher education
item.description: Mika Kennedy and Pamela Sertzen, professors in the Center for the Study of Culture, Race and Ethnicity at Ithaca College published an article in the Ethnic Studies Pedagogies Journal in December 2025. item.title: Editorial: Black History Month is imperative to understanding all of history
item.description: Black History Month is imperative to understand the true history of the United States. While this month is not limited to the history of Black Americans, amidst the pushback against diversity, equity and inclusion policies, celebrating the achievements of Black Americans while equally acknowledging their unique experiences throughout our nation’s history is crucial. item.title: IC, Do You Copy? | A Stranger Things Season 5 Recap
item.description: Welcome to the bonus fifth episode of IC, Do You Copy?, a limited-series podcast where host Tamar Wachi sits down with special guests to recap and review seasons of the hit Netflix original series "Stranger Things." In this episode, Tamar is joined by first-year student Abigail Chesman to discuss their thoughts and feelings on the show's fifth and final season. item.title: Luc Besson’s ‘Dracula’ is soul-suckingly bad
item.description: “Dracula: A Love Tale,” directed by Luc Besson and based on Bram Stoker’s 1897 novel, was originally released in France in July 2025, having its wide theatrical release in North America Feb. 6. While the film description claims to be a Gothic romantic fantasy, in actuality, it has no idea what it wants to be. item.title: Men’s wrestling continues dominant streak through senior day
item.description: On Feb. 13, Beneath the bright lights of the Ben Light Gymnasium, the No. 22 Ithaca College men’s wrestling team punctuated its home schedule with a 29-9 dual meet performance against the Wilkes University Colonels that honored its past while solidifying its postseason future. item.title: Empire State Collegiate Championship reflects themes of the gymnastics season ahead of nationals
item.description: The Ithaca College gymnastics team traveled to SUNY Cortland to compete in the Empire State Collegiate Championship on Feb. 14. The Bombers placed No. 5 out of six teams, behind Long Island University, Cornell University, SUNY Brockport, Cortland and ahead of Utica University.
